question: Should OpenClaw add a native custom ASR/STT backend abstraction, and should the first slice bridge native capture to existing Gateway/media/provider contracts rather than adding a standalone native HTTP endpoint preference?
rationale: The missing capability is source-proven, but implementation choices affect native app UX, provider ownership, credentials, private-network trust, fallback behavior, and whether this becomes a new config surface or a reuse of existing provider contracts.

options.title: Design Gateway-backed native ASR seam
options.body: Keep Apple/Android platform speech as the default, start with one approved native flow such as macOS Push-to-Talk or mobile dictation, and route provider-backed transcription through existing Gateway media or realtime provider controls.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical trackers
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad umbrella but require platform-specific issues like macOS PTT and WebChat dictation to carry implementation and proof separately.

options.title: Defer native custom ASR
options.body: Keep native voice capture on platform speech until maintainers have a broader voice-input provider plan and security model.

recommendation.title: Design Gateway-backed native ASR seam
recommendation.body: Keep Apple/Android platform speech as the default, start with one approved native flow such as macOS Push-to-Talk or mobile dictation, and route provider-backed transcription through existing Gateway media or realtime provider controls.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest sampled history is in native voice and Talk configuration paths, and the product decision needs native app scope ownership before provider details can be finalized.
